note: Profile fit is close to textbook: a 33-year-old Marine officer climbing in rank with organisational responsibility, 5'6" and 150 lb at a self-reported 15-16% body fat, wanting 10-12% and explicitly framing it as getting ahead of a slide rather than a rescue — 'I'm not in a bad position, but... I need to get ahead of this.' He fails only on the income test, and fails it hard and for structural rather than attitudinal reasons: single income, two young children, US childcare costs, a cross-country relocation and a deliberate cash buffer for a planned career change. He is the case the ICP observation about payment plans describes — the profile the company wants, priced out by a lump sum in a bad month rather than by unwillingness to pay.
